```{r setup, include=FALSE}
has_seurat <- requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE) &&
    utils::packageVersion("SeuratObject") >= "5.0.0"
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = has_seurat)
```

`import_from_seurat()` uses the optional `SeuratObject >= 5.0.0` package.
Full Seurat and SingleCellExperiment are unnecessary for this path. It supports
ordinary in-memory `Assay5` and legacy `Assay` containers through SeuratObject
5.
This is data interoperability with Seurat; it does not run Seurat integration,
batch correction, normalization, or marker testing.

Supply the original full raw count library, with responses in one assay and
guides in another. Each assay must have exactly one unsplit `counts` layer
covering all its features and every cell in the whole Seurat object, in order.
Seurat v5 permits assay-specific cell universes and split count layers; this
adapter rejects these cases instead of silently selecting the first matching
layer, intersecting cells, or joining batches. If needed, explicitly join
layers
upstream and verify the resulting full feature/cell library first. Missing
counts,
data-only assays, noninteger/negative/nonfinite counts, backed matrices, and
partial count layers are rejected. Integer-valued normalization cannot be
identified automatically; the caller must establish raw-count provenance.

```{r import-seurat}
library(sceptre)
library(SeuratObject)
data("lowmoi_example_data")
x <- lowmoi_example_data
metadata <- x$grna_target_data_frame
# Seurat replaces underscores in feature IDs. Make a transparent source mapping
# before construction, then keep and supply the actual stored identifiers.
metadata$original_grna_id <- metadata$grna_id
ids <- paste0("guide", seq_len(nrow(x$grna_matrix)))
rownames(x$grna_matrix) <- metadata$grna_id <- ids
s <- CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = Matrix::Matrix(x$response_matrix, sparse = TRUE),
    meta.data = x$extra_covariates, min.cells = 0, min.features = 0)
s[["gRNA"]] <- CreateAssay5Object(
    counts = Matrix::Matrix(x$grna_matrix, sparse = TRUE),
    min.cells = 0, min.features = 0)
object <- import_from_seurat(s, metadata, "low", covariates = "batch")
```

The selected response assay defaults to `RNA` and guides to `gRNA`. The active
Seurat assay and variable-feature selection do not determine imported counts.
Guide metadata must cover the complete stored guide order. Selected cell
metadata must follow the count cell order. Named physical layers must agree
with Seurat's feature/cell maps; unnamed layers necessarily use those maps as
their identity authority. The adapter cannot reconstruct names already changed
or features already filtered upstream. To identify mitochondrial genes from a
feature metadata symbol column, supply `response_name_column`. Otherwise
feature
IDs with the usual `MT-` prefix determine mitochondrial fractions.

Full-library depth and detected-feature summaries are computed before choosing
pairs or running QC. Counts remain raw and unchanged. Covariate names that
collide
with computed summaries reject. The shared external-assignment API accepts
binary guide-by-original-cell calls, with the same canonical vector-ID and
low/high-MOI rules described in the SingleCellExperiment vignette.

```{r analyze-export-seurat}
pairs <- data.frame(response_id = rownames(x$response_matrix)[1L],
                    grna_target = metadata$grna_target[1L])
object <- set_analysis_parameters(object, discovery_pairs = pairs,
    formula_object = ~ log(response_n_umis), control_group = "complement",
    side = "left", resampling_approximation = "no_approximation")
object <- set_grna_assignments(object, x$grna_matrix >= 5,
    "demonstration raw UMI >=5 caller")
object <- run_qc(object, response_n_umis_range = c(0, 1),
    response_n_nonzero_range = c(0, 1), p_mito_threshold = 1,
    n_nonzero_trt_thresh = 3L, n_nonzero_cntrl_thresh = 3L)
object <- run_discovery_analysis(object, print_progress = FALSE)
returned <- export_results_to_seurat(object, s)
Misc(returned, slot = "sceptre")$results$run_discovery_analysis
```

The broad QC ranges and threshold caller are demonstration settings, not
general
recommendations. Validate the upstream calling method and run calibration for
your intended analysis. Successful import is not scientific validation.

Results live in `Misc(returned, slot = "sceptre")`, with original and retained
cell IDs, full-library covariates, current pair tables and provenance. Each
response can have several target associations, so results are not flattened to
one cell or feature metadata value. Export checks exact imported response
counts
and identities, requires current completed results, rejects existing `sceptre`
miscellaneous information, and preserves the input object. Save/reopen using
RDS.

For an actual fresh-process pipeline roundtrip from the full bundled example:

```{bash pipeline-seurat, eval=FALSE}
R_LIBS=/absolute/isolated/library \
    Rscript tools/interoperability/seurat-roundtrip.R \
    /absolute/schema3-pipeline-checkout /tmp/new-seurat-roundtrip
```

The source helper uses the same pipeline external-assignment companion as SCE.
Both analysis and assignment configuration sections remain absent to preserve
the prepared calls. It compares direct/pipeline results at tolerance zero,
checks original-object ownership and saves a returned Seurat object locally.
This exercises R-stage serialization/execution, not a scheduler or container.
